newsitem.title: NIGERIA: NIGERIA TO START REFINERY MAINTENANCE-OIL MINISTRY.
newsitem.headline: NIGERIA TO START REFINERY MAINTENANCE-OIL MINISTRY.

text.p: Nigeria's oil ministry on Wednesday said it would begin the repair of ailing refineries to try to alleviate the chronic fuel shortages that sporadically paralyse the country's economy.
The work would begin with the northen Kaduna plant bfore moving on to Port Harcourt and then Warri refineries, oil minister Dan Etete said in a speech delivered on his behalf in Lagos.
"Necessary arrangement has been set in motion to start the turnaround maintenance of Kaduna," Etete said.

"It is our hope that Port Harcourt refinery maintenance will start immediately after Kaduna is back on stream, that is if necessary funds have been released. Hopefully then Warri turnaround maintenance should start after Port Harcourt."

The independent Vanguard newspaper on Wednesday reported that the finance ministry had released $145.8 million to state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp for priority projects, which include refinery rehabilitation.

Lack of funds and maintenance have hit Nigeria's refineries which have a combined capacity of 445,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil; Kaduna (110,000 bpd), New Port Harcourt (150,000 bpd), Old Port Harcourt (60,000 bpd) and Warri (125,000 bpd).
Shortages have forced Nigeria to import fuel despite the fact that it pumps over two million bpd of crude oil.
